ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A wooden block with a mass of $0.5\mathrm{kg}$ slides up a smooth inclined plane at an angle of $30^{\circ}$ with a speed of $10\mathrm{m/s}$ (assuming the plane is sufficiently long), and $g$ is taken as $10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$.

1. What is the momentum of the wooden block at the end of 1s?
2. What is the change in momentum of the wooden block in 3 seconds?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A wooden block with a mass of $0.5\mathrm{kg}$ slides up a smooth inclined plane at an angle of $30^{\circ}$ with a speed of $10\mathrm{m/s}$ (assuming the plane is sufficiently long), and $g$ is taken as $10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$. 1. What is the momentum of the wooden block at the end of 1 s? 2. What is the change in momentum of the wooden block in 3 s?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached diagrams show a block on a smooth inclined plane. The plane rises to the right, and the angle between the plane and the horizontal is labeled 30°. The initial velocity arrow v0 is drawn along the plane upward, so take the positive direction as up the incline. Reasoning: Since the plane is smooth, the only acceleration along the slope is the component of gravity down the slope: a = -g sin 30° = -10 × 1/2 = -5 m/s². With initial velocity v0 = 10 m/s, the velocity is v(t) = 10 - 5t. At t = 1 s: v = 10 - 5(1) = 5 m/s, so p = mv = 0.5 × 5 = 2.5 kg·m/s. At t = 3 s: v = 10 - 5(3) = -5 m/s. The change in momentum from the initial moment to 3 s is Δp = m(v3 - v0) = 0.5(-5 - 10) = -7.5 kg·m/s.
